about: For each public item of today's kkt-config, where it lives in the proposed map and whether it stays a constant or becomes injected (a field of a settings struct the program fills). Format and fixed facts live in the crate that owns them, private there or public when others use them; tuning values are settings fields; operator settings and defaults are in kkt-settings or the program; Nothing stays in kkt-config: it goes, and its last items live with their owners. An item other crates read only in their tests is test-visible, public behind `testing`; one they use in their own code is public. Crates are named as the proposed map names them; used_by and test_only name today's users.

limits.note: Limits was what kkt-settings gathered from flags, the config file and defaults; its fields split into per-crate settings structs, each checked and worded for the run record by its own crate. In phase 9 kkt-settings and the gathered Limits go: kkt-server's ServerSettings holds the settings of what it builds or passes on (the formatter's and the page's), and the program fills kkt-rules' Settings, for the Rules it builds, and kkt-backup's

parts.doc: kkt-rules' share of today's Limits: name_pack, default_limit, max_limit, max_body_bytes, the name, purpose, description, note, announcement, memory and lane lengths, the lane description's length (today's MAX_LANE_DESCRIPTION_CHARS), sends_per_minute, registrations_per_minute, max_agents, default_wait, max_wait, waiting_grace, member_preview and purpose_preview_chars; problems() gives every bad setting it holds, each with the setting's name and which of its own checks found it, and record_lines() its own name and value lines for the run record (step 9.1).

kkt-mcp-formatter's share of today's Limits: max_response_bytes; problems() gives every bad setting it holds, each with the setting's name and which of its own checks found it, and record_lines() its own name and value lines for the run record (step 9.1).

kkt-web's share of today's Limits: page (a PageLimits of web_page_messages and web_member_excerpt_chars: step 6.2) and web_session_lifetime (session_lifetime, since the sessions are kkt-web's: step 6.1), and the lengths its forms check (channel name, purpose, description), which the program fills from kkt-rules' since kkt-web must not depend on kkt-rules; problems() gives every bad setting it holds, each with the setting's name and which of its own checks found it, and record_lines() its own name and value lines for the run record (step 9.1).
